As far as historical precedent goes and how the game pans out: Yes and No.

Early on in WP we had very silly things happen (tree armies, duck marriage, and undead stalin to name a few) but after a while a more serious and political tone took over. The US broke up and in the wake of that power was rebalanced. A few large nations ended up on the end of the chopping block (China as a big debacle) and other nations coalesced from other regions (California+Mexico created a lasting union) while other more 'background' nations held down their regions. (With the power vacuum of the US falling apart, Brazil became a pillar of South America, Turkey became a naval power and Australia became an empire.) I think because of the Civ-like nature of these games, outcomes become slightly skewed to the less realistic, but certain instances (War in China) struck me as very odd and very real. We used to have people see our posts in /r/New and think it was real until they looked into the subreddit itself. I hope that answers your question.
